description: The bar chart illustrates the negative log probability of per-specialty medical terms as predicted by the Mistralv0.2-Base model, comparing performance across six clinical specialties: Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics, and Pediatrics. The vertical axis represents “Negative log probability,” ranging from approximately -22 to -27, with lower values indicating higher model confidence (i.e., more probable predictions). The horizontal axis groups bars by specialty, with each group containing six bars corresponding to the six specialties, colored as follows: light blue for Mistralv0.2-Base (a reference or baseline model), and shades of orange and brown for Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics, and Pediatrics respectively. Within each specialty group, the bars represent how well the model predicts terms from that specialty — for example, in the “Cardio” group, the “Cardio” bar (light orange) is among the lowest (most confident), while the “Pediatrics” bar (dark brown) is among the highest (least confident). A consistent pattern across all specialty groups is that the model performs best (lowest negative log probability) on terms from its own specialty and worst on Pediatrics terms, which consistently show the highest negative log probabilities across all groups. The chart visually emphasizes that the model’s performance is highly dependent on the alignment between the input specialty and the target term’s specialty, suggesting that clinical specialty data plays a significant role in the model’s predictive behavior.
